# Hardware, Fieldbus & Actuator Reference {.unnumbered #sec-appendix-hardware}

This appendix provides a consolidated physical reference for the electronic, communication, and electromechanical hardware substrates encountered in Physical AI deployments and educational laboratory kits.

---

## 1. Dual-Brain System Configurations

Physical AI architectures decouple stochastic cognitive reasoning from deterministic safety enforcement across two distinct physical compute domains:

| Architecture Tier              | Educational Dual-Brain Kit (Arduino UNO Q)                          | Industrial Robotics Platform (e.g., KUKA / Franka)              | Autonomous Vehicle Compute Unit (e.g., Drive Orin)              |
|:-------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cognitive Brain (System 2)** | Qualcomm DragonBoard / Multi-core Cortex-A (Debian Linux)           | Industrial PC / Intel Xeon + NVIDIA RTX GPU (Ubuntu RT-PREEMPT) | NVIDIA Tegra Orin SoC (12x Cortex-A78AE + Ampere GPU + DLA)     |
| **Safety Enforcer (System 1)** | ARM Cortex-M4 / STM32 (FreeRTOS / Bare-Metal @ 1 kHz)               | ARM Cortex-R5 / TI TMS570 (SafeRTOS / ASIL D MCU @ 1 kHz)       | Infineon AURIX TC397 / TC4x (TriCore Safe Lockstep MCU @ 1 kHz) |
| **Inter-Brain Physical Bus**   | Shared SRAM Mailbox via RPMSG / OpenAMP                             | Isolated PCIe Gen 4 with DMA or Dedicated Ethernet              | High-speed PCIe Gen 4 x4 + Dedicated Dual-SPI Heartbeat         |
| **Safety Watchdog Mechanism**  | Hardware GPIO pulse toggle ($t_{\text{timeout}} \le 3.0\text{ ms}$) | Independent Dual-Channel Safety Relay (ISO 13849 PLe)           | Hardware System Safety Manager (SSM) with Failsafe Watchdog     |
| **Power Consumption (TDP)**    | $5\text{--}15\text{ W}$                                             | $150\text{--}450\text{ W}$                                      | $60\text{--}250\text{ W}$                                       |

## 2. Robotics Fieldbus & Interconnect Comparison Matrix

| Fieldbus Protocol                     | Physical Layer                     | Max Payload                   | Bitrate / Bandwidth                                | $P_{99}$ Latency                       | Hardware Determinism & Jitter                        | Typical Physical AI Function                            |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| **SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface)** | 4-wire CMOS (SCLK, MOSI, MISO, CS) | Arbitrary byte stream         | Up to $50\text{ Mbps}$                             | $<10\,\mu\text{s}$                     | Hard Real-Time ($<0.1\,\mu\text{s}$ jitter)          | On-board IMUs, joint encoders, ADC chips                |
| **CAN 2.0B**                          | Differential pair (ISO 11898-2)    | 8 bytes                       | $1.0\text{ Mbps}$                                  | $0.5\text{--}2.0\text{ ms}$            | Priority-arbitrated ($<50\,\mu\text{s}$ jitter)      | Legacy automotive sensors, low-speed motor drives       |
| **CAN-FD**                            | Differential pair                  | 64 bytes                      | $5.0\text{--}8.0\text{ Mbps}$                      | $100\text{--}350\,\mu\text{s}$         | Priority-arbitrated ($<20\,\mu\text{s}$ jitter)      | Robot joint drives, battery management, chassis control |
| **EtherCAT**                          | 100BASE-TX Ethernet                | Up to 1486 bytes (on-the-fly) | $100\text{ Mbps}$                                  | $50\text{--}125\,\mu\text{s}$          | Hard Real-Time ($<1\,\mu\text{s}$ distributed clock) | High-speed multi-axis industrial motor synchronization  |
| **MIPI CSI-2**                        | Differential D-PHY / C-PHY         | Uncompressed frame            | Up to $10\text{ Gbps}$                             | Frame rate ($16\text{--}33\text{ ms}$) | Deterministic DMA push                               | Edge vision and depth sensor raw ingestion              |
| **PCIe Gen 4**                        | Point-to-point differential lanes  | Packets up to 4 KB            | $16\text{ GT/s}$ per lane ($2.0\text{ GB/s/lane}$) | $1.5\text{--}5.0\,\mu\text{s}$         | High-throughput DMA (Subject to UMA contention)      | Host AP to GPU / NPU accelerator tensor handoffs        |

## 3. Actuator Transmission Mechanics & Reflected Inertia

In physical actuation, a motor's rotor inertia $J_{\text{rotor}}$ is amplified by the square of the gear reduction ratio $N$:

$$J_{\text{eff}} = J_{\text{load}} + N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$$

| Transmission Type            | Gear Ratio Range ($N$) | Backdrivability & Compliance | Reflected Inertia Impact ($N^2$)          | Torque Density ($\text{N}\cdot\text{m/kg}$) | Typical Physical AI Application                              |
|:-----------------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Direct Drive**             | $1:1$                  | Perfect (No friction)        | Minimal ($1\times$)                       | Low ($1\text{--}3$)                         | High-bandwidth haptic teleoperation, direct-drive turntables |
| **Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD)** | $4:1\text{--}10:1$     | High (Low friction)          | Low ($16\times\text{--}100\times$)        | Moderate ($15\text{--}30$)                  | Dynamic legged locomotion (quadrupeds), agile humanoids      |
| **Planetary Reducer**        | $10:1\text{--}50:1$    | Moderate                     | High ($100\times\text{--}2500\times$)     | High ($30\text{--}60$)                      | Mobile robot wheels, industrial robotic base joints          |
| **Strain Wave (Harmonic)**   | $50:1\text{--}160:1$   | Low / Non-backdrivable       | Severe ($2500\times\text{--}25600\times$) | Very High ($80\text{--}150$)                | High-precision articulated robot arms, surgical manipulators |
| **Cycloidal Drive**          | $30:1\text{--}100:1$   | Moderate / Shock-resistant   | High ($900\text{--}10000\times$)          | Exceptional ($100\text{--}200$)             | Heavy-payload manipulator wrists, industrial AGVs            |

## 4. Power Delivery Network (PDN) & Voltage Droop

When a deep neural network accelerator switches from an idle state to full-load matrix tensor computation, the step current demand $\Delta I$ creates a transient voltage droop across the power distribution network:

$$\Delta V_{\text{droop}} = L_{\text{trace}} \frac{dI}{dt} + R_{\text{trace}} \Delta I$$

* **The Brownout Risk:** If an edge GPU draws a $\Delta I = 80\text{ A}$ current step in $10\text{ ns}$ across an unconditioned parasitic inductance $L_{\text{trace}} = 0.5\text{ nH}$, the transient droop $\Delta V = 40.0\text{ V}$ can collapse a shared $48\text{ V}$ DC bus below the minimum operating threshold of the microcontroller's low-dropout (LDO) regulator ($<3.3\text{ V}$), triggering a local processor reset.
* **Architectural Mitigation:** Physical AI systems must employ galvanic DC-DC power isolation and dedicated bulk decoupling capacitors ($C_{\text{decouple}} \ge \frac{\Delta I \cdot \Delta t}{\Delta V_{\text{allowable}}}$) between cognitive accelerators and real-time microcontroller buses.

---

## 5. Actuator Thermal Rise & Resistance Drift

The electrical resistance of copper motor windings increases linearly with operating temperature:

$$R_{\text{winding}}(T) = R_0 \left( 1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}} (T - T_0) \right)$$

where $\alpha_{\text{Cu}} \approx 0.00393\text{ K}^{-1}$ at $T_0 = 20^\circ\text{C}$.

* **Consequence for Control:** As a motor heats from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to its maximum thermal limit ($120^\circ\text{C}$), coil resistance increases by $+39.3\%$. Under voltage-mode control, the achievable phase current and output torque drop proportionally by $28.2\%$, violating nominal kinematic reachability assumptions unless closed-loop Field-Oriented Current Control (FOC) is enforced at $>10\text{ kHz}$.
